ads_ratio.reason: ADS_RATIO_MISSING: 20-F filer - EDGAR per-share figures are per share (common and preferred carry identical EPS) while the Nasdaq price is per ADS; each ADS represents exactly one preferred share, so the ratio is 1.0 and no scaling applies, but the declaration is required so make_score does not refuse on DATA_GAP:ads_ratio.
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-13), Item 9 / listing description: the NYSE-traded Level II ADSs (symbol GGB) are equivalent to one preferred share of Gerdau S.A. (GGBR4); the cover registers Preferred Shares, no par value, each represented by American Depositary Shares on the NYSE

moat_against: Commodity long/special steel: no pricing power - steel prices are set globally and Brazilian prices are capped by imports (import share ~22% of the domestic market in 2025 vs a far lower historical average); gross margin fell from 26.6% (FY2021) to 11.4% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json

Returns are cyclical, not structural: roic_proxy in fundamentals.json swung from -6.7% (FY2016) to 41.7% (FY2021) and back down to 4.4% (FY2025) - a through-cycle record that does not stay above the cost of capital
Scale rivals everywhere: Nucor, Steel Dynamics and Commercial Metals in the US, ArcelorMittal and CSN in Brazil; low-cost import supply (China-origin) disciplines every market Gerdau serves

BRL and Brazil macro exposure: reporting currency BRL converted at period-end rates, Brazilian rates high for prolonged periods, and the controlling family structure (Metalurgica Gerdau) adds a governance layer
Capex intensity is rising into the trough: FY2025 capex $1.251B (R$6.85B incl. intangibles) on the Miguel Burnier mining build, against FY2025 conservative OE of only $179.9M (R$985M)
moat_for: Americas long-steel scale: largest long-steel producer in the Americas, 11.6 Mt shipped in 2025 (+5.9%), with integrated scrap-based mini-mills - scrap is the low-cost, flexible feedstock in North America

North America earnings engine: 62% of FY2025 consolidated adjusted EBITDA (company 4Q25 release), ~90 days of order backlog and resilient data-center/renewables demand, in a market protected by US trade measures

Vertical integration upstream: captive iron ore (Miguel Burnier expansion, ~R$1.1B potential annual EBITDA at full ramp per the 4Q25 release) and scrap collection lower delivered cost through the cycle

Balance-sheet discipline: FY2025 net debt/adjusted EBITDA 0.76x (company release), below the company's own 1.5x policy ceiling, with gross debt of R$14.18B (20-F Notes 15/16: loans and financing R$9.77B + debentures R$4.41B) against equity of R$53.80B in fundamentals.json

Shareholder returns through the trough: FY2025 dividends + buybacks R$2.4B (182.3% of the bylaws payout measure, company release); preferred share count fell from 1,377,906,016 weighted (FY2023) to 1,285,879,767 (FY2025) in the 20-F EPS note
moat_justification: Weak moat, 3/10. Gerdau has real scale advantages - largest long-steel producer in the Americas, scrap-based mini-mill cost position in North America (62% of FY2025 adjusted EBITDA), captive iron ore expanding at Miguel Burnier, and a disciplined 0.76x net debt/EBITDA balance sheet - but none of it converts into pricing power or through-cycle returns: gross margin compressed from 26.6% (FY2021) to 22.8% / 16.4% / 13.7% / 11.4% across FY2022-25 and roic_proxy (fundamentals.json) fell from 41.7% (FY2021) to 29.3% / 18.2% / 12.5% / 4.4% over the same years, with FY2016 at -6.7%. A steelmaker whose ROIC only clears its cost of capital at cycle peaks, whose home market is import-capped, and whose product is a global commodity has a weak moat. A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years.
name: Gerdau S.A.
one_liner: Americas long-steel scale with a weak commodity moat 3/10 - the normalized base OE of $0.42/share is a mid-cycle construct (FY2025 printed $0.09 on peak capex and crushed Brazil spreads); at $5.08 the weighted IRR is 10.21% by numbers (Tier C), but on each fiscal year's own filed diluted share count the median base is $0.4068/share and the weighted IRR replays to 9.89% - final Tier D via tier_override, IV@15% $3.14 by numbers ($3.01 on the corrected count); on the corrected count it clears 15% only below ~$3.01.
sector: Industrials / Steel (long & special steel, Brazil & North America)

shares_override.reason: DATA_GAP:shares - diluted shares missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 in EDGAR companyfacts; the only filed counts are dei outstanding counts for the COMMON class alone (717,782,619 at Dec 31, 2025 per the 20-F cover, vs 1,283,097,330 preferred shares issued), which cover barely a third of the capital and are on the wrong basis for consolidated OE. Gerdau allocates earnings equally per share to common and preferred (same basic and diluted EPS for both classes in the EPS note), and the NYSE ADS is a preferred share, so the matching denominator for consolidated owner's earnings is the EPS note's total diluted count (common + diluted preferred). The engine applies this single FY2025 value to every missing period: FY2025 is exact; FY2024 OE/share is computed on 2,012,732,574 instead of its own filed 2,099,379,471 (overstates FY2024 OE/share by ~4.3%) and FY2023 on 2,012,732,574 instead of 2,109,593,750 (overstates by ~4.8%), and the same value also fills FY2022, which is outside the median window; the direction makes the median base slightly generous, not conservative, and is disclosed in analysis.md.
shares_override.source: Form 20-F for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-03-13), Note 24 Earnings per share, Diluted table: common shares outstanding 718,139,434 plus preferred diluted total 1,294,593,140 (weighted-average preferred 1,285,879,767 + potential increase from long-term incentive plans 8,713,373) = 2,012,732,574 total diluted shares for FY2025; the same table gives FY2024 total 2,099,379,471 (720,527,899 + 1,378,851,572) and FY2023 total 2,109,593,750 (720,527,899 + 1,389,065,851), and diluted EPS is identical for common and preferred shares (R$0.69 / R$2.18 / R$3.56)

tier_override_reason: Numbers tier is C at a 10.21% weighted IRR, but that IRR rests on the single-value shares_override: the engine applies the FY2025 total diluted count (2,012,732,574) to every missing year, while the same FY2025 20-F Note 24 table files FY2024's own total diluted count at 2,099,379,471 and FY2023's at 2,109,593,750. On each year's own filed count the 3-yr median base is $0.406841/share (FY2024 OE $854,113,196 / 2,099,379,471; FY2023 $0.551412, FY2025 $0.089379 — FY2024 remains the median year), and replaying the run's unchanged scenario inputs on that base gives a 9.89% weighted IRR and IV@15 of $3.01 — Tier D. A per-year share series is outside the override layer (single-value, fill-only) and a base_override built on the filing's counts is outside the run-outputs bound, so the correction is taken as this quantified tier_override; the by-numbers C at 10.21% remains printed in score.json.
